top_story_title: Cisco email gateway zero-day reported as patched and exploited - confirm against the Cisco advisory before acting
top_story_summary: The only network-adjacent item in this 24-hour window is a weekly roundup from Help Net Security whose headline states that Cisco has patched an exploited zero-day in its email gateway. The roundup itself carries no CVE identifier, no affected version list and no fixed release, and the remainder of its content (a Revolut data breach, an open-source Windows driver hunting tool) is outside this digest's scope.
top_actions: Open Cisco's Security Advisories page and locate the email gateway advisory referenced by this headline; record the CVE and the fixed release from Cisco directly.
Inventory Cisco email security appliances by model and running version before planning any upgrade.
Confirm the appliance management interface (HTTPS/SSH/API) is not reachable from the internet and is restricted to a management VLAN or out-of-band network.
Enforce MFA on appliance administrative accounts and remove shared local admin logins.
Review appliance admin logins and configuration changes in the SIEM for the period before patching - exploitation predates the fix by definition.
executive_summary: A single item reached the digest in this 24-hour window: a weekly news roundup stating that Cisco has patched an exploited zero-day in its email gateway.
No CVE, affected version or fixed release is given in the source - the Cisco advisory itself must be consulted before any change window is scheduled.
No firewall, VPN gateway, router, switch, wireless or load-balancer advisories appeared in this window.
No new AI-related network item and no vendor AI defence announcement in this cycle.

headlines.title: Week in review: Cisco patches exploited email gateway 0-day, Revolut breach
headlines.summary: A weekly security roundup reports that Cisco has patched an exploited zero-day in its email gateway, without naming a CVE or a fixed release.
